newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - Aug 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - Aug 19.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Sri Lankan political and business stories prepared for Reuters by NewsWatch, Colombo Tel/Fax: 94-1-735182 Internet: lucien@eureka.lk.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SRI LANKA MULLS LAWS TO TACKLE SEA PIRACY

Sri Lanka is considering bringing in new legislation to tackle sea piracy. Deputy Solicitor General Kolitha Dharmawardena, who heads the committee to recommend new laws, said piracy was not treated as a distinct criminal offence at present. Acts of piracy are dealt with under the penal code as theft or robbery. The proposal is a sequel to worries among international shipping community that Sri Lanka is not a safe port for transhipping.
DISPLACED PEOPLE DEMONSTRATE IN EASTERN TRINCOMALEE

Some 800 displaced people in the eastern port city of Trincomalee launched a protest fast demanding they be sent back to their homes in the northern Jaffna peninsula. They are part of some 8,000 people waiting to go to Jaffna after shipping services were cancelled early last month following attacks on civilian ships by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).
The Virakesari newspaper said the fast had been called off after protesters were given assurances by governemnt officials they immediate steps will be taken to send them back to Jaffna.
GOVERNMENT MULLS DISCIPLINARY ACTION AGAINST TRUANT MPs

The ruling People's Alliance government has decided to take strict disciplinary action against its parliament deputies who abstain from the house without a valid reason. According to a senior minister, this decision has been taken after the government found itself in difficult situations due to low attendace of its deputies and ministers during parliamentary debates.
ADMONITION TO SOLVE PROBLEMS OF TAMILS EXPEDITIOUSLY

The government has issued a directive to all concerned departments that priority should be given to finding problems faced by displaced Tamils who are living in Colombo, its suburbs and elsewhere in the Indian Ocean island.
